A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LCS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original latent-space PCA analyses, color-observation experiments, GenEval/PRECISE evaluations, and qualitative color interventions.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds multi-object interventions, preservation comparisons, alternative color metrics, and PCA analyses of additional models.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 substantially revises the specified core color mapping. Polygon-edge encoding becomes spherical interpolation of centered anchor directions, with a separately interpolated radius and revised saturation normalization. These are non-equivalent encoder/decoder definitions used by observation and intervention; the surrounding Type I/II interpolation framework remains.

E1.justification: The existing GenEval, wall-color, and PRECISE coverage is retained. v2 adds qualitative scenarios requiring simultaneous, differently colored interventions on adjacent or overlapping objects (Appendix C), plus a complex crystal-ball scene involving reflections and smoke (Figure 7). This modestly extends task requirements and scene coverage.

E2.justification: Best-of-N, ColorPeel, and ReNO were already evaluated in v1 Table 4 and remain in v2 Table 5. v2 adds IP-Adapter to quantitative evaluation. It also substantially broadens structure-preservation comparisons beyond prompting to Best-of-N, ColorPeel, ReNO, and IP-Adapter through new Table 4 and revised Appendix I/Figure 15.

E3.justification: The reported PCA sample count changes from 512 to 400, and PCA evaluation expands to SD3.5, FLUX.2, and Qwen-Image. New protocols assess SSIM/LPIPS on the existing 300-image PRECISE subset, HCL/CIELAB color errors, and later interventions with cleaner bounding boxes. These substantially expand evaluation settings; the sample-count revision alone does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of simultaneous interventions, cross-model LCS structure, and fine-detail preservation using jointly improved bounding boxes and later intervention (Appendices C, L, and H). It also expands qualitative structure comparisons and examines lighting coherence. These supplement the retained intervention-type/timestep study and color-subgroup analyses with substantial new diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Figure 15 newly identifies the prompt-based qualitative comparison as using the same seed, adding a seed-control disclosure. The four-seed main PRECISE evaluation, one-seed reduced comparison, and fixed plain-image prompt/seed pairs remain unchanged. Neither version reports confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerous LCS and baseline scores change in Tables 1–2 and matched appendix tables. Table 2 changes local/global GenEval accuracy from 70%/73% to 68%/72%, natural-image local color error from 17 to 14, and plain-image global error from 9 to 11. Table 3 is unchanged. New comparative, color-metric, and qualitative results substantially extend the evidence. The PDFs do not explain all score revisions, so these are not established same-procedure performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 substantively changes the mathematical construction through an anchor center, vector-angle hue interpolation, a hue-dependent equatorial radius, and spherical encoding. Section 3.1 also replaces the reconstruction-plus-KL background objective with an LPIPS/KL/adversarial min–max formulation. The LCS–HSL bijection remains assumed rather than newly proved.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: an HSL-like three-dimensional FLUX color subspace, latent color observation, and training-free mechanistic color intervention. Additional validation does not redefine these stated core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly explains that early interventions can alter fine details and semantics, sometimes improving realism but hindering editing, and discusses mitigation through later intervention and cleaner boxes. v2 also qualifies cross-architecture generality as preliminary and narrows the early-observation superiority claim to 'sometimes.' The principal mechanistic interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents a preservation variant using approximately timesteps 20–25 with cleaner bounding boxes and supplies prompts for new qualitative cases. It clarifies mask compatibility while retaining the existing layer-18 segmentation approach. Code-access information, color definitions, existing prompt/seed pairs, and timestep calibration arrays remain unchanged; improved-box construction is not specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds the FLUX.2 reference and connects it to broader architectural applicability. The related-work narrative and novelty positioning otherwise remain stable. Renamed author entries, publication updates, and consolidated duplicate references correspond to existing works rather than substantive additions or removals.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the VAE preliminaries, geometric mapping, and mask usage. Interpolation is named Type ⋆, method labels become LCS, and Section 5.6, appendix headings, and an Impact Statement are added. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds multi-object, preservation, cross-model, and geometric illustrations, plus Tables 4 and 8. It replaces the earlier structure-comparison grid, revises observation panels and Figure 7, corrects Figure 4's intervention labels, and marks the selected setting in Figure 6. This substantially expands and revises visual presentation beyond relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a clearer geometric specification, corrects intervention labels and an overbroad early-prediction claim, and strengthens validation with additional preservation controls and cross-model checks. These improve understanding and empirical support. However, widespread score replacements remain unexplained and some new settings lack implementation detail, limiting the additional confidence they provide. The net improvement is supported by clearer exposition and evidence, not uniformly better performance.
